subject: Romanian catalogue — what exists today
body: Jubilujah does carry Romanian-language albums: the Nations · Romanian category holds 10 albums by Zburdalnicii, 8 of them playable with audio (IX401RO, IX402RO, IX403RO, IX405RO, IX418RO, IX423RO, IX424RO, IX425RO) — roughly 90 tracks. A second Romanian artist, Veselia Copiilor, is registered with no albums released yet. Important and honest caveat: every Romanian album currently in the catalogue is CHILDREN'S music (the Romanian edition of the Party Giggles line). There is no Romanian-language adult worship in the catalogue today. More translation work is in progress — the repository holds prepared translation briefs for 40 languages including Romanian.

review: I did not know this existed. I have been running the children’s work here for six years and every single week I choose between songs my kids will actually sing and songs my mother would recognise, and this is the first time I have not had to choose. “Cântecul Mântuirii” came on and I had to put the phone down. My daughter is nine. She heard three bars of “Cucurigu al Răscumpărării” and laughed — at the rooster, not at the Romanian — and then she sang the chorus. In Romanian. She has never done that without being asked. I played it again after she went to bed and I cried in the kitchen like a person with no self-control. Doamne ferește, I am not usually like this about a children’s album. Please make more.

I will be honest that the Hawaiian and the Romanian together confused a couple of the older ones — one boy asked me which country this was from and I did not have a clean answer. Still four stars because they danced and because “Stropii Mei Sunt Lauda Mea” is a lovely line.

review: This one is the deepest of the Romanian set. “Sunete de Shofar și Prăjituri de Păstor” put the shofar in front of children as something joyful rather than something strange, and my church has a hard time explaining our roots to kids who have only ever been American. I used it for the whole of Easter week. The older women in the church heard it through the door and came in. That has never happened before.

subject: CORRECTION — the Romanian catalogue is far larger than first reported
body: The earlier notice was materially wrong and is superseded, not deleted. Verified against catalog-manifest.json: there are 31 PLAYABLE Romanian-language albums, not 8. Eight are the children's line (Zburdalnicii, filed under Nations · Romanian). The other twenty-three are ADULT worship by the Inspire Family, filed under the inspire category by artist: Amir 2, Caleb 2, Eliana 2, Elias 2, Imani 2, Jubilee 2, Melody 2, Nova 2, Santiago 2, Tahoma 2, Zariah 1, Zev 2. Examples: MDIM1005RO Du-ma acasa, MDIM1008RO Minuni Obisnuite, JEIM1069RO Jubilujah, EAIM1001RO Singurul Nume de Care Vei Avea Nevoie, ZEIM1022RO Hesed Care Nu Se Opreste. A trilingual track also exists on IMX505 (Mihaiela Norica). Nineteen further languages carry -XX coded editions (AR DE FR HE HI IT JA KO NL PL PT BR RU SV TH TL TR VI ZH).
root_cause: The Nations · Romanian category surfaces ONLY the 8 children's albums. The 23 adult Romanian albums are filed under inspire by artist and never appear in the Romanian browse path. A Romanian speaker browsing by language sees children's music and concludes there is nothing else — which is exactly the wrong conclusion this persona and its author both reached.
